summary_plain: The BASS investigation burned various solid materials like fabric sheets, wax candles, and plastic spheres inside the International Space Station's Microgravity Science Glovebox. Researchers studied how flames spread over these materials in microgravity under different airflow conditions and tested the effectiveness of nitrogen as a fire suppressant. Understanding how solids burn in space without gravity's buoyant flow helps improve spacecraft fire safety and material selection.
summary_expert: Conducted aboard the International Space Station inside the Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG) using the small flow duct hardware (SPICE), the BASS (PSI-26) investigation performed 121 tests examining the burning and extinction characteristics of solid fuels including Japan wax, Nomex, PMMA, SIBAL, Ultem, and paraffin wax in candle, fabric, sheet, slab, and sphere geometries. The investigation evaluated concurrent-flow and opposed-flow configurations across variable airflow speeds reaching up to 40 cm/s, alongside nitrogen-based flame extinguishment assessments. Results indicated that concurrent-flow flame spread rate increases linearly with flow speed, whereas opposed-flow flame spread rate increases with flow to a maximum around 10 to 15 cm/s and then decreases at higher speeds, and tests revealed that local application of a suppressant jet entrains air and sustains the flame even when ambient airflow is turned off.

key_findings.text: For concurrent flow, the flame spread rate increases linearly with airflow speed, and the flame base spread rate reaches a steady state for all points shown.
For opposed flow, the flame spread rate increases with flow to a maximum when the flow speed is around 10 to 15 cm/s and then decreases at higher speeds.
Local application of a suppressant is not adequate for flame extinguishment because the local jet entrains air and sustains the flame even when the ambient airflow is turned off.
Materials in microgravity with adequate ventilation can burn as well if not better than the same material in normal gravity with all other conditions being identical.

earth_applications: Improving strategies for extinguishing accidental fires
Developing combustion computational models used in the design of fire detection and suppression systems on Earth
